settings.subtitle: Manage panel access, security credentials, notification delivery, and form dictionaries.
settings.basic_desc: These settings control how the panel appears and is accessed in the browser.
settings.panel_title_desc: Shown at the top of the sidebar and in the browser title.
settings.panel_access_desc: The panel only listens on HTTPS. Changing the port or random path restarts the service automatically to apply it; the panel is briefly unreachable during the restart.
settings.cloudflare_toggle_desc: Enable when the panel sits behind Cloudflare. Recognizes Cloudflare's edge and uses CF-Connecting-IP as the real visitor IP.
settings.reverse_proxy_toggle_desc: Enable when the panel sits behind Nginx, Caddy, or another reverse proxy. When off, X-Forwarded-For is not trusted.
settings.trusted_proxies_hint: One IP or CIDR per line. A same-host Nginx/Caddy usually keeps 127.0.0.1 and ::1; if the reverse proxy is on another machine, enter that machine's IP.
settings.domain_ssl_desc: Bind a domain to the panel and pick a certificate mode based on your deployment:
settings.ssl_mode_hint:
Auto-issue (Let's Encrypt) → the panel owns the whole machine, no reverse proxy/CDN, port 80 must be free
Self-signed / uploaded certificate → use when Caddy, Nginx, or Cloudflare sits in front
settings.cloudflare_note_body: You don't need auto-issue — visitors see Cloudflare's edge certificate. Set the SSL/TLS mode to Full with a self-signed certificate, or Full (strict) with an uploaded Cloudflare Origin CA certificate. Cloudflare's proxy forwards to the origin on the same port the visitor used by default; to reach it without a port, either free up 443 on the origin or use Cloudflare Origin Rules to forward it to the panel's actual port.
settings.update_desc: Panel version check/update, auto-update policy, and system package updates.
settings.auto_update_desc: Off by default. When enabled, updates happen automatically only within the configured time window, and only to stable releases.
settings.system_update_desc: Checks for apt-upgradable system packages. One-click update runs apt update && apt upgrade -y directly on the server.
settings.updating_in_progress: Update in progress, do not close this page
settings.backup_desc: Generate a packaged backup (.tar.gz) of the database and encryption keys, optionally emailed to the admin. The keys decrypt saved server/website passwords — without them, those passwords can't be decrypted after a restore.
settings.auto_backup_desc: Off by default. When enabled, generates local backups on a fixed schedule and keeps a set number of recent ones.
settings.send_to_admin_email: Email the backup to the admin address
settings.this_run_result_desc: Status of the manual backup run.
settings.restore_desc: Restore the database and keys directly from an existing local backup or an uploaded backup file (.tar.gz). Before restoring, the current database and keys are automatically saved as a .pre-restore backup, and the panel restarts automatically during the restore.
settings.restore_from_existing_prefix: Restore from an existing local backup: open “
settings.restore_from_existing_suffix: ” and pick the file to restore.
settings.or_upload_restore: Or restore by uploading a backup file:
settings.cli_fallback_hint: If the panel service itself can't start (e.g. disaster recovery after reinstalling the OS), use the command line instead:
settings.cli_step1: Copy the backup file (.tar.gz) to the new server
settings.security_desc: BasicAuth, panel login, and the view password are all managed here.
settings.view_password_desc: Used to view saved SSH passwords, server panel passwords, and website panel passwords. Required again each time.

settings.account_security_desc: BasicAuth adds an extra login layer to the panel. You'll need to log in again after changing panel login info.
settings.basic_auth_off_warning: Turning this off removes a layer of protection. If it's just to skip typing a password, keeping it on with a simple username/password is still safer than disabling it entirely.
